report.summary:
Here's what I've learned about you. Riverbend has been doing this work since 2016. You run hospital-based intervention and street outreach across two precincts, with a team of 19. You are an established group with real systems that your team uses. Your Planning and Financial Management are at the Developing stage. Your Fundraising and your Monitoring, Learning and Evaluation are at the Emerging stage. This is a learning tool, not a grade. It shows where you are today and where to build next.

You are strong in planning and money basics. You keep written work plans for the next 6 to 12 months and check your progress against them. You review financial reports with leadership and the board, you track spending by program and funding stream, you hold reserves, and you do an independent audit every year. You also have a written fundraising plan, and you have funding that lasts beyond one year. On the data side, your programs have defined outcomes, your team uses standard tools, and you review data together and share it with funders and partners. Those are real foundations.

You are a little weaker in a few connected places. Most of your money is restricted government funding, so it is hard to see clearly what is confirmed and what is still pending. Your data work is mostly counting what you do, and not every staff member is trained to collect and use data the same way. Your board works well but could use more finance know-how. If I were you, I would start with two things. First, build a clear 12-month picture of your funding, with confirmed money in one column and pending money in another. Second, train your staff to collect and use data the same way every time. These two steps are small and doable. They also make every later funding conversation stronger.
